Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

profile noun

a side view of a face

also in profile, side view, silhouette, profile picture, a profile (of someone’s life)

classical

Plin. NH 35.90: oblīquam namque fēcit
Plin. NH 35.56: catagrapha … hoc est oblīquās imāginēs
M-O s.v. silhouette: profile

imāgō oblīqua

noun phrase: imāgō, imāginis f.

a profile, a side view (of a portrait)

Pliny’s phrase for the portrait seen from the side, which Lewis & Short renders “a side-likeness, profile” (s.v. oblīquus). Oblīquus is slanting, sidelong: oblīquō capite, with the head turned (Plin. NH 8.88).

Other words

  • catagrapha, catagraphōrum n. pl. — profile drawings, side views

    noun, second declension, plural · also used · classical · Plin. NH 35.56 (Lewis & Short, s.v. catagraphus)

    The Greek painters’ term, which Pliny explains with oblīquae imāginēs; a word for art history, not for everyday use.

  • adumbrātiō, adumbrātiōnis f. — a sketch, an outline; a short profile of a person

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Cic. Or. 103 (Lewis & Short): a sketch, outline; M-O s.v. silhouette: adumbrātiō vītae, a biographical sketch

    For a written profile of someone, Morgan–Owens gives adumbrātiō (alicujus) vītae. Classically a sketch, and also a mere show or pretence (Lewis & Short).

Examples

  • pīnxit et Antigonī rēgis imāginem alterō lūmine orbātī prīmus excōgitātā ratiōne vitia condendī; oblīquam namque fēcit, ut, quod deerat corporī, pictūrae deesse potius vidērētur

    he also painted King Antigonus, who had lost an eye, and was the first to think of a way of hiding defects: he painted him in profile, so that what the body lacked might seem rather to be lacking in the picturePlin. NH 35.90

See also picture, face.

SourcesLewis & Short: obliquus · Lewis & Short: catagraphus · Lewis & Short: adumbratio · Lewis & Short: imago

Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. forms: silhouette: profile.
